brief: Brent crude's surge past $109/bbl on inflation fears pushed the 10-year US Treasury yield above 5% for the first time since October 2023, triggering an aggressive rate-expectation repricing: money markets now price nearly four Fed hikes (including this week's meeting) and four ECB hikes by July 2027, plus five BoE hikes over the next 12 months. That hawkish shift lifted DXY to 99.6 and pushed EUR/USD down to 1.1538, driving heavy selling in EM currencies and equities (MXN, PLN, HUF, CLP hit hardest). Equities were also hit by a separate AI-sector selloff after tech leaders called for slower AI development, dragging the Nasdaq 100 down 1.2% and the SOX over 5%; gold fell more than 2% below $4,300/oz. The note frames Wednesday's FOMC decision as the swing factor for risk assets into year-end. In European rates, the 10Y OAT hit its highest level since 2008 (4.47%) and the Italian BTP-Bund spread widened, even as ECB year-end hike pricing held steady despite the oil shock. The note also reports, without further argument: an accelerating Canada CPI print, a weaker-than-expected China retail sales figure, and single-name items including Monte dei Paschi's bank bids, a Realty Income-KKR European JV, and SoftBank's OpenAI-linked loan.
